nodes.label: Telegram Desktop Test Harness
nodes.rationale: One packed scenario and one app launch is the default. Splitting into multiple launches is justified only by an incompatible process-lifetime requirement (a startup-only setting or persisted state the first flow necessarily contaminates); 'the scenario is large' or 'a smoke run is simpler' are explicitly rejected as reasons to split, because fragmenting the scenario loses shared fixture setup and diagnostic context.

nodes.label: Stage Contract (run/until/then)
nodes.rationale: Separates readiness observation (until, which must stay pure and never encode an expected product result) from action (run) and assertion (then/captureAndInspect). Keeping falsifiable outcomes out of until prevents a real product mismatch from being mislabeled as an opaque timeout.

nodes.label: Runner::actOnWidget
nodes.rationale: Polls a resolver and optional readiness predicate, keeps a QPointer to the exact accepted object, and invokes the action once, removing both the eager-.run crash and the 'resolve again in .then' race.

nodes.label: Live Widget/Action Publication (PublishLiveWidget/PublishLiveAction/ReadLiveWidget/ReadLiveAction/InvokeLiveAction)
nodes.rationale: Publishing the exact constructed object or action at its real production seam is preferable to guessing which control (e.g. a RoundButton) belongs to a layer-owned, repeated, or asynchronously-replaced widget.

nodes.label: FindAll/FindFirst/FindVisible RTTI Finders
nodes.rationale: Telegram custom widgets generally do not declare Q_OBJECT, so findChildren<Ui::CustomWidget*>() may return unrelated widgets blindly cast to that type; these finders enumerate real QWidget descendants and apply C++ RTTI safely instead.

nodes.label: Chat Message List Resolution (HistoryWidget/HistoryInner vs HistoryView::ChatWidget/ListWidget vs AdminLog::InnerWidget)
nodes.rationale: A chat's message list is not necessarily one named widget: the legacy stack (HistoryWidget+HistoryInner), the modern stack (HistoryView::ChatWidget+ListWidget, which also backs replies threads, forum topics, and monoforum/Saved Messages sublists), and the admin log (AdminLog::InnerWidget, which implements HistoryView::ElementDelegate itself and constructs no ListWidget) each differ. A scenario must resolve the list from the section that constructs it and prove the candidate owns the message, rather than assume one fixed widget name.

nodes.label: Input Helpers (Click/TypeText/CommitText/PressKey/Drag/Wheel/Settle/ForceWindowActive/ClickBoxButton)
nodes.rationale: All input helpers synchronously dispatch real Qt events and drain postponed work, targeting the exact widget that owns the event route -- because Ui::InputField's wrapper does not override keyPressEvent and an ignored key event propagates up the parent chain rather than down into the child QTextEdit that actually owns the text.

nodes.label: Capture and Visual Assertion Helpers (CaptureWidget/CaptureMappedRect/captureAndInspect/CaptureViaWindow/CapturePopupMenu/PaintingLayerRoot)
nodes.rationale: Choosing the narrowest helper that captures the real paint owner avoids blank or partial grabs caused by animation caches, transparent fade-in proxies (toasts), or scroll-viewport clipping. captureWidget/captureAndInspect reject missing, hidden, empty, near-uniform and invalid transparent-root frames, so readiness must identify current content rather than assert the expected pixels itself.

nodes.label: Test::Check Details Argument
nodes.rationale: Check's third argument is an observation, not a failure excuse: it is printed on both the PASS and FAIL verdict lines so a green log states what each check was judged against and a passing run can be audited without rerunning it. Failure-only text stays conditional at the call site so the passing line remains exactly 'TEST_RESULT: PASS: <what>'.

nodes.label: Media Fixture Playability Probe
nodes.rationale: Metadata alone (song/audioFile flags, plausible duration) cannot distinguish an undecodable synthetic upload from real playable music, so a fixture is accepted only after the run has watched it play: candidates are really opened through the production path and the first whose TrackState::position strictly advances while length>0 is accepted and reused everywhere, rather than re-derived per stage.

nodes.label: Scenario Teardown Before Quit
nodes.rationale: A scenario that deliberately leaks its State to outlive a stage owns the release of everything that State holds; a leaked State whose two rpl::lifetimes were never released kept observers subscribed to session-owned streams while ~Main::Session tore those streams down, producing a SIGSEGV after TEST_COMPLETE with no assertion line and a 0-byte minidump. A final teardown stage fixed it, but that stage itself is skipped by a timeout or the watchdog, so its having run must be confirmed.

nodes.label: Test::Probe / DiscriminatingScan
nodes.rationale: Round-trip and enumeration oracles must correlate records by key rather than by list position or wall-clock slice, and a scan must be validated against a known-present control before a zero result is certified as absence -- otherwise a structurally-guaranteed 'found=0' measures nothing.

nodes.label: Test Helper Module Catalog (test_*.h)
nodes.rationale: Each helper module owns a self-test proving its own refusal/acceptance contract. Searching this catalog before writing a new local helper is required, because a reimplemented local copy carries none of the refusals the shared helper accumulated -- one overlay rebuilt grab-check-save by hand after CaptureWidget had already refused blank and hidden targets for months.
